question.text: Meridian Special Situations Fund (Cat II AIF) is set up as a trust. During documentation, the Manager's tax counsel emphasises that the Trust Deed must make the beneficiaries' shares 'determinate' at inception. If the trust is deemed indeterminate under Section 161(1A) of the ITA, what is the primary adverse consequence?

answer.text: The trust loses SEBI registration automatically.
The trust is taxed at 12.5% LTCG on all income.
Unitholders lose the right to claim TDS credit.
The trust becomes liable to tax at the Maximum Marginal Rate (MMR) on its ENTIRE income at the fund level, defeating the pass-through benefit intended by Section 115UB.

explanation.text: The Logic: For a Category I/II AIF set up as a trust, tax counsel typically insists that the trust be irrevocably settled with determinate beneficiaries and determinate shares so that the trust qualifies for clear pass-through tax treatment. If the trust were treated as indeterminate (beneficiaries or their shares not identifiable from the trust deed), the representative assessee taxation framework in the Income-tax Act subjects such trusts to tax at the Maximum Marginal Rate on the trust's income at the fund level. That outcome would defeat the pass-through intent of the special AIF tax regime by taxing income at the fund instead of allowing it to flow to investors. The Trap: Indeterminacy under the Income-tax Act has no automatic SEBI registration consequence, so SEBI registration is not lost. A flat LTCG rate on all income is not the consequence of indeterminacy — the consequence is taxation at MMR at the fund level. TDS credit at the investor level operates through a separate mechanism and is not the primary consequence of indeterminacy either. Note: The cited workbook pages support the points that an AIF trust should be irrevocably settled and determinate for clear tax treatment, and that Category I/II AIFs receive pass-through treatment under the relevant section of the Income-tax Act with MMR treatment for specified business income. The specific Section 161(1A) consequence (entire trust income taxed at MMR at the fund level where the trust is indeterminate) is not spelled out in the cited chapter. The framing above is general Income-tax Act / trust-law knowledge rather than a direct workbook citation.
